title: How to Get a Personal Loan for a Low CIBIL Score?
summary: RBI's directions set no minimum CIBIL score for a personal loan, so each lender decides. See what to check first, what helps, and how to spot risky loan apps.
body_markdown:
## Can you get a personal loan with a low CIBIL score?


Sometimes, but each lender decides, and a low score usually means a smaller amount, a higher rate or a refusal. CIBIL says so itself: "The decision to lend is solely dependent on the lender and CIBIL does not in any manner decide if the loan/credit card should be sanctioned or not."


A credit score is a three-digit number, from 300 to 900, that a credit bureau works out from your credit report. A credit bureau is a company registered with RBI that keeps credit records and produces your report and score. Your credit report is the record of your loans, cards and repayments that the bureau holds.


CIBIL is one of four bureaus. RBI's list names CRIF High Mark, Equifax, Experian and TransUnion CIBIL.[What a credit score is and how it is calculated](https://koshex.com/blog/credit-score) covers the basics. A personal loan here means an unsecured one, which is a loan with nothing pledged against it.


## What is the minimum CIBIL score for a personal loan?


RBI sets no minimum in the directions it issues to banks and bureaus. Every credit bureau in India scores you between 300 and 900, because RBI requires that scale. Each lender sets its own cut-off.


CIBIL says a score above 700 is generally considered good. It also says that the closer your score is to 900, the higher the chances of your application being approved. Those are CIBIL's words about its own score, not a rule for lenders.


Equifax adds that lenders typically have different score cut-offs depending on which bureau is providing the score. So a lender may read a score from one bureau differently from a score from another.


You will see tables online that promise an "approval chance" for each score band. They are not rules. The cut-off that counts is the one your lender sets.


## What should you do before applying?


Get your free credit report first and read every account and enquiry on it. Every calendar year, each of the four bureaus must let you have one free full credit report, score included. It matches the detailed version lenders get. Ask for it on the bureau's website; the link must be on its home page.


An enquiry is the entry a lender's check leaves on your report. Every application leaves one. Experian says a hard enquiry might temporarily lower your score, and advises checking your own score before you apply. A bureau does not report an application that was declined, so a refusal itself is not recorded, but the enquiry it caused is.


Your score is worked out from your report, so a wrong entry can change it. If you find one, the steps to dispute it are in[the credit score guide](https://koshex.com/blog/credit-score) .


Lenders also weigh the EMIs you already pay. EMI stands for equated monthly instalment, the fixed amount paid each month that covers interest and part of the loan.[Why personal loans get rejected](https://koshex.com/blog/common-reasons-for-personal-loan-rejection-tips-to-avoid) covers that side.


A lender that refuses you because of your report must tell you why in writing within thirty days, under RBI's 2006 regulations.


## Does a co-applicant or a smaller loan help?


Both can change a lender's answer, though the lender still decides. A co-applicant is a second person who applies for the loan with you, and they add a second income and a second credit record. A smaller amount means a smaller EMI. You can see how an amount changes the instalment in the[personal loan calculator](https://koshex.com/calculators/personal-loan-calculator) .


A guarantor is a person who agrees to repay if the borrower does not. The same loan then shows on that person's report. RBI requires a bureau to capture the details of co-borrowers and guarantors, and a report shows loans taken as borrower, co-borrower or guarantor.


That has a cost for whoever you ask. CIBIL says a guarantor on any form of loan is equally responsible for repayment, and that any default by the principal applicant will affect the guarantor's score as well. It also says that on a co-signed or jointly held account, you are held equally liable for missed payments.


For the wider picture of how to apply, see[how to get a personal loan](https://koshex.com/blog/how-to-get-a-personal-loan) .


## Can you borrow against your FD, mutual funds or gold instead?


Yes, if you hold something a lender accepts as security, and the limit then follows what you pledge. A secured loan is backed by something you pledge, such as gold or fund units. The lender's own policy still decides what score it wants.


Take Revathi, a 38-year-old self-employed tailor in Coimbatore. Her score fell after she missed card payments last year. She holds equity fund units and her family's gold jewellery. These figures are assumed, for illustration only.


Say her equity fund units are worth ₹2,40,000. RBI's directions to banks set a loan-to-value ceiling of 75 per cent for mutual funds other than debt funds. Loan-to-value, or LTV, is the most a lender may lend as a share of what you pledge. So a bank could lend her at most ₹1,80,000 against those units, or less under its own policy. RBI's ceiling for debt mutual funds is 85 per cent. NBFCs set their own LTV for fund units. An NBFC is a lender that is not a bank but is registered with RBI.


Say the gold in her jewellery is valued at ₹1,00,000. RBI's rules for banks and NBFCs allow gold loans only against jewellery, ornaments or coins. The gold is valued at the lower of its 30-day average price and the previous day's price, counting gold content only. The ceiling is 85 per cent for a loan up to ₹2.5 lakh, so the most she could borrow is ₹85,000. If she repaid everything in one payment at the end, that ceiling would cover the principal plus the interest due at maturity.


Above ₹2.5 lakh, RBI requires a bank or NBFC to run a detailed credit assessment, including the borrower's repayment capacity.


A fixed deposit (FD) is money placed with a bank for a set period at a rate fixed when you open it. RBI tells banks not to sanction advances against the term deposits of other banks. SBI's YONO page, updated on 21 May 2025, describes an overdraft of up to 90 per cent of FD value at 1 percentage point above the relevant time deposit rate. That is one bank's product on one date.[Loans against fixed deposits](https://koshex.com/blog/do-banks-offer-loans-against-fixed-deposits) covers how a bank lends against your own deposit.


[Can digital gold be used for a loan?](https://koshex.com/blog/can-digital-gold-be-used-for-loans) explains which gold a lender accepts. How a loan against mutual funds compares with a personal loan is covered in[the mutual fund loan guide](https://koshex.com/blog/get-loan-against-mutual-funds) . For a home loan,[home loan eligibility](https://koshex.com/blog/looking-for-ways-to-increase-your-home-loan-eligibility) explains how lenders decide.


None of these routes sits outside the credit system. Each is a loan like any other: the lender reports it to credit bureaus, and missing interest payments can hurt your credit score.


## How long does it take to improve a low score?


There is no fixed time. Since July 2026, banks and NBFCs report to the bureaus on four dates a month, with data as on the 9th, 16th, 23rd and the last day. Expect a payment you make to appear on your report in about two weeks.


Older entries stay as history. Bureau records are kept for a minimum of seven years under RBI's 2006 regulations, and closed accounts are shown after live ones.


A settled account is one where the lender accepted less than the full amount owed because the borrower could not pay. If you settled a loan with a bank, that bank must wait at least 12 months before lending to you again (except farm loans).


[Why your CIBIL score is low, and how to improve it](https://koshex.com/blog/reasons-for-having-a-low-cibil-score-how-to-improve-it) covers what moves a score and in what order.


## Are loans without a CIBIL check safe?


Treat that promise as a reason to check who is lending. RBI's rules say lending through digital lending apps is reported to the bureaus, irrespective of its nature or tenor. A regulated lender reports an app loan like any other.


Behind a legal loan app there is always a lender RBI regulates, either a bank or a registered NBFC, and the app and that lender's website must name it. You can look up an NBFC on RBI's list of registered NBFCs.


RBI also publishes a list of lenders' digital lending apps, as the lenders report them. Being on it is not an approval: RBI says it does not verify the list, and inclusion is no registration, authorisation or endorsement.


The full checklist is in[how to check if a loan app is RBI-regulated](https://koshex.com/blog/loan-apps-rbi-regulated) .
